subject: science
notes: Sea otters use rocks to crack open the shells of clams and other prey.
Chimpanzees push thin sticks into termite mounds to pull out termites to eat.
New Caledonian crows shape twigs into hooks to pull insects out of holes in trees.
Scientists once thought that only humans used tools.
stem: The student wants to make a generalization about tool use among animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Scientists once thought that only humans used tools.
choices.B: Sea otters use rocks to crack open the shells of clams and other prey.
choices.C: New Caledonian crows shape twigs into hooks and use them to pull insects out of holes in trees.
choices.D: Several kinds of animals, including sea otters, chimpanzees, and crows, use tools to get food.

explanation.why: A generalization is a broad statement drawn from several examples. The notes give three different animals that each use a tool to get food. Only one choice combines these examples into one general statement about animals.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reports an old belief about humans. It does not make a general statement about animals that use tools.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This describes one animal only, so it is an example, not a generalization.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This describes one animal only. It is detailed, but it is still a single example.
explanation.D: Correct. It draws on all three examples to make a broad statement: several kinds of animals use tools to get food.
